title: Is MYP Physics a Good Subject Choice?
summary: Is MYP Physics right for you? Compare its content, assessment, workload, mathematics, future pathways, and key subject-selection questions.
body_markdown:
### Is MYP Physics a good subject choice?


**MYP Physics is a good subject choice if you enjoy explaining physical systems, applying mathematics, interpreting data, and conducting investigations.** It provides useful preparation for physics, engineering, technology, mathematics, architecture, and some medical sciences. However, it is not automatically the best science for every student, and choosing it only because it appears impressive is rarely sensible.


Your decision should reflect your interests, mathematical confidence, learning style, future plans, and school-specific options. The MYP is a framework rather than one identical worldwide syllabus, so physics courses can differ between schools.


### How MYP subject selection works


The official[IB overview of the MYP curriculum](https://ibo.org/programmes/middle-years-programme/curriculum/) identifies eight subject groups, including **sciences** . In Years 4 and 5, schools may use subject-group flexibility within IB rules, allowing students to study courses from six groups where appropriate.


Physics is normally taught within sciences, but the IB does not require every school to offer it separately. The[IB overview of MYP sciences](https://ibo.org/programmes/middle-years-programme/curriculum/science/) explains that biology, chemistry, and physics may be organized as separate courses or integrated science. RevisionDojo's explanation of[how schools customize MYP subject choices](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/choice-of-subjects-how-schools-customize-myp-for-local-needs) provides additional context.


Before choosing, ask your coordinator:


- Is physics separate or part of integrated science?
- Which topics does the school cover?
- Are there entry-grade requirements?
- Is external MYP eAssessment offered?
- How much practical work is expected?
- Is the course recommended for DP Physics?


These local details matter more than a generic course description.


### What you study in MYP Physics


Schools select and sequence content according to the MYP framework and local requirements. Common areas include forces and motion, energy, thermal physics, electricity, magnetism, waves, atomic physics, and space. RevisionDojo's[MYP Physics lessons and study guides](https://www.revisiondojo.com/myp/myp-physics/learn) show a representative topic range, although your school's course may differ.


Physics requires you to connect descriptions, diagrams, measurements, graphs, and equations. For example, one task might ask you to describe motion, interpret a distance-time graph, and calculate speed using speed equals distance divided by time. Students who enjoy moving between these forms of information often respond well to the subject.


### How MYP Physics is assessed


MYP Physics is not assessed through calculation tests alone. The official[MYP sciences subject brief](https://www.ibo.org/globalassets/new-structure/brochures-and-infographics/pdfs/myp-brief-sciences-en.pdf) describes four equally weighted criteria, each assessed through achievement levels from **1 to 8** .


Criterion Main focus Typical task


**A: Knowing and understanding** Applying scientific knowledge Explaining concepts or solving problems


**B: Inquiring and designing** Planning investigations Identifying variables and designing methods


**C: Processing and evaluating** Analyzing results and methods Graphing data and evaluating errors


**D: Reflecting on the impacts of science** Connecting science with society Evaluating an energy technology


This balance matters. A student who can use formulas but dislikes experimental design, data evaluation, or scientific writing may find the course different from what they expected. Optional external MYP eAssessment is available in physics and integrated sciences, but participation depends on the school. School-based assessment remains important throughout the programme.


### Reasons to choose MYP Physics


Physics may suit you if you:


- Enjoy topics such as motion, energy, electricity, waves, or space
- Can work with algebra, ratios, graphs, units, and proportions
- Prefer applying ideas rather than memorizing facts alone
- Like practical investigations and analyzing imperfect results
- May consider DP Physics or a quantitative future pathway
- Will practise when a problem is not immediately obvious


The course develops transferable skills, including designing fair tests, checking units, interpreting evidence, evaluating limitations, and communicating logical explanations.


MYP Physics can also make the transition to DP Physics easier. It is not a universal IB prerequisite, however, and schools may establish their own progression requirements. RevisionDojo's guide to[taking DP Physics after MYP Physics](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/taking-dp-physics-after-myp-physics) distinguishes helpful preparation from formal eligibility.


### Reasons MYP Physics may not suit you


Physics may be a weaker choice if you strongly dislike algebra, quantitative data, graphs, or unfamiliar problems. Investigations also demand patience because students must plan variables, collect measurements, present results, draw conclusions, and evaluate limitations.


Do not assume physics is inherently more valuable than biology, chemistry, or another subject. If your interests and future plans relate more directly to biological, environmental, or chemical sciences, another option may fit better. A course in which you remain engaged is usually more useful than a prestigious choice that leaves you continually disengaged.


### A practical decision checklist


Consider whether you can honestly agree with these statements:


- I am curious about how physical systems work.
- I can manage algebra, graphs, ratios, and unit conversions.
- I am willing to practise problems regularly.
- I can explain reasoning instead of providing only an answer.
- I am comfortable learning from experimental errors.
- Physics supports a future pathway I may consider.
- The course fits my overall workload.


This is not an admissions test. Discuss your answers with science and mathematics teachers, who can evaluate your current habits and readiness. If possible, inspect a unit outline and attempt several tasks from an[MYP Physics Questionbank](https://www.revisiondojo.com/myp/myp-physics/questionbank) . Actual problems provide better evidence than the subject's reputation.


### Common subject-choice mistakes


Do not choose physics simply because your friends are taking it. Their abilities, interests, and future plans may be different. Strong mathematics is helpful but does not guarantee success because physics also requires conceptual explanation, investigation, evaluation, and communication.


Equally, one difficult topic does not prove that physics is the wrong choice. Consider whether solving challenging problems feels worthwhile once you understand them. Finally, check your school's progression rules and possible university expectations, especially if you are considering engineering or physical sciences.


### Conclusion


MYP Physics is a strong choice for students who enjoy quantitative problem-solving, experiments, scientific models, and evidence-based explanations. Base your decision on your school's actual course, your mathematical foundation, your willingness to practise, and the pathways you want to preserve.


If you select physics, RevisionDojo's[MYP Physics resource hub](https://www.revisiondojo.com/myp/myp-physics) and[MYP Physics flashcards](https://www.revisiondojo.com/myp/myp-physics/flashcards) can support review, while the Questionbank helps test whether you can apply ideas independently.
